name: Steel arm harness
description: Steel plates for one arm: a forearm guard, a rounded elbow cup and an upper-arm plate, buckled on with leather straps. A row of strange marks is etched along the forearm.
notes: Laid out flat along x, wrist at -x, open side down, 560 mm long: a tapering forearm plate, an elbow cop with a side wing and an upper-arm plate, each with buckled brown leather straps, and five dark etched marks along the forearm plate as the magic made material (`steel-blued`). One guard for one arm: the `arms` slot has no side, so a pair needs a sided slot or two items, as batch 090's arm guard notes. The open shells lie apart along the arm with their straps out. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Shimmering wool arming mittens
description: Thick quilted mitts of a silvery wool that shimmers with faint colours, with long flared cuffs. Lighter and cooler than ordinary wool, and an arrow struggles to get through them.
notes: Laid flat side by side, backs up, fingers towards +z, each mitt 270 mm from cuff to fingertip: quilted in lines along the back and cuff, the flared cuff bound at its mouth. Built on `g.glovePair` with `mitten: true`. The pair lies spread flat with thumbs out. Slot `hands`, as earlier clothing batches named it. Protection values are a judgement for wool quilting made to stop arrows: better against points than ordinary padding, fair against cuts and blows. The silvery wool is `cloth-shimmer`, with quilting, binding and laces in `cloth-purple` so the cloth reads as iridescent; an iridescent cloth finish that shifts hue with the view angle would suit it better. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
